## Monitor counts (no switch) {#sec-ch10-counts}

### Summary

Some events are counted, not booked: how many faces a floor lifted, how many Riemann solves fell back. The
monitor keeps one integer counter per named event. A producer hands it a mask; the masks of a stage are summed
together at the stage's end without atomic additions, so the counts are exact and the same under capture.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Integer counts per event name, summed per stage from the producers' masks ([-@eq-ch10-counts-sum]).

**Data.** `counters` (int64), `minima` (FP64, $+\infty$ when unset), `retry_flags` (int32); the stage's masks in
one fixed buffer.

**Placement.** Masks posted inside the stage; summed by `end_stage`.

**Activation.** Always; the names are declared at the register's reset.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact (integer sums); counts never enter a budget row.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer of this section.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathbf b$ is the stage's count buffer, $\mathbf b[0] = 0$ followed by the masks; $C$ is a
counter's cumulative-sum view of $\mathbf b$.

### Derivation

Let $C[j] = \sum_{i \le j}\mathbf b[i]$ be the integer cumulative sum of the buffer. A mask posted at offset $o$ with
$n$ elements counts

$$
C[o+n] - C[o],
$$ {#eq-ch10-counts-sum}

The sum is {{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp RegisterMonitor::flush_counts >}}.

and a counter's stage count is the sum of this over its masks. All terms are integers, so the sum is exact in any
order.

### Numerical method

A reduced count (a zero-dimensional tensor) adds into its counter at once. A mask or a vector is copied into its slot
of the stage's buffer; the slot pattern (which counter, how many elements) is built eagerly at the first post and
reused. `flush_counts`, called by `end_stage`, takes one cumulative sum, gathers the segment ends of every counter
(padded to the largest number of segments with the leading zero), adds the differences into the counters, and
zeroes the buffer. The face-floor and Riemann-event masks of the sweep are posted this way. No scatter-add is used;
an FP64 scatter-add would add atomically on CUDA. The buffer is fixed storage registered with the state store, so a
captured combine reduces what the replayed advance wrote. Where the flush falls is shown in
@fig-ch10-register-order.

Walk-through: `count` looks the name up (an undeclared name stops with an error), then either adds a reduced count or
copies a mask into its slot; `end_stage` calls `flush_counts`.

### Limits

The counts are per accepted step only through the rollback (@sec-ch10-rollback). A slot pattern built inside a
capture is not allowed. Switch combinations are in @sec-ch12-matrix.
